Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list, and sorry for the delay. Short version up front: for Private (VPC) deployments we operate the inference control plane but customers retain full ownership and operational control of primary storage and keys when configured that way. I attached a short commitments doc and a dataflow diagram for visibility.

Answers at a glance (I put bullets to match your spreadsheet):
- Snapshot/backup ownership: If customer configures storage in their account (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) Redwood can be configured to write only to customer-owned buckets. Redwood does not retain independent long-term copies in our managed storage for that configuration. We may create transient snapshots for live troubleshooting but these are short-lived (operational TTL) and are scoped to customer-owned storage.
- Retention windows / geo: Snapshot retention and region selection are configurable. We recommend a default 7-day operational snapshot TTL but can set stricter customer-controlled policies and geo-lock snapshots to a single region in the cloud provider.
- Deprovisioning evidence: At termination we provide a deletion report consisting of object deletion logs, S3 delete markers, and a checksum summary for objects removed. We can also coordinate a notarized signed attestation for enterprise contracts.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS keys are supported. When you supply and manage keys, Redwood never holds plaintext keys; we rely on KMS APIs and do not do key handoffs. If you require key destruction confirmation (for short-lived keys used for migration), we can provide KMS audit entries and an operational certificate that keys were revoked.
- Audit trail: We record operations in an append-only audit log (control plane) which includes who initiated a deletion request and the associated request id. For customer-managed storage we also reference cloud-provider object lifecycle logs to create a correlated timeline.

I'll double-check a couple of implementation details with infra/legal and follow up with the specific log fields and example artifacts. Meanwhile attaching: redwood-residency-commitments-2026.pdf and redwood-private-vpc-dataflow-diagram.pdf.

—Marissa

Marissa — quick confirmations from infra side:
- Our serving runtime does maintain a short-lived KV cache and occasionally creates a checkpoint in ephemeral block storage for fast restarts. Those checkpoints are lifecycle-managed and deleted automatically; they are not copied into Redwood-managed S3. We should disclose that ephemeral checkpoints may exist for up to 24 hours by default unless the customer sets a shorter TTL.
- We do not create any separate long-term backups by default. Any backup outside customer buckets requires explicit opt-in and contractual acknowledgement.
- Geo-lock: yes — when the storage is customer-owned we can set snapshot targets and lifecycle rules to a single region; we need the region specified at onboarding.

Hi Anna — following up with the implementation confirmations from our infra and legal teams. Apologies for the longer turnaround; wanted to get concrete artifacts for you.

Summary of commitments (items we can include in SOW):
- Ownership: When customer-provisioned object storage is selected, primary data is stored in your account and Redwood does not maintain independent long-term object stores.
- Ephemeral checkpoints: The runtime may create ephemeral checkpoints (ephemeral block storage / KV caches) to support availability; default maximum TTL is 24 hours. We will include the option to reduce TTL to 0–4 hours if MediSync requires tighter limits.
- Snapshots & retention: Snapshot targets and lifecycle rules are configurable and can be geo-locked to a single region. Default operational snapshot TTL is 7 days unless contractually adjusted.
- Deletion evidence: At deprovisioning we will provide a deletion bundle that includes: cloud-provider object deletion logs (delete markers / lifecycle operations), a checksum manifest for deleted object keys, and correlated control-plane audit entries linking deletion request ids to actor ids. For enterprise contracts we can provide a signed attestation letter.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS/HSM keys are supported. Redwood never persists plaintext keys. We will provide KMS audit entries demonstrating key revocation when applicable.
- Auditability: We will export correlated, append-only audit logs (control plane) and link to cloud-provider object lifecycle logs to show a deletion timeline. We can provide example log excerpts and field definitions prior to SOW signature.
